teams.synopsis: Dominating for the second week in a row — the 49ers stars' health is the only real cloud.
teams.blurb: Dominating for the 2nd week in a row. <mark class="hl-player">Worthy</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Reed</mark> were disappointing in Week 2, but that was expected. <mark class="hl-player">Kamara</mark> could be a top-5 running back while healthy... again. Injuries to both 49ers stars may bring some down weeks to the team, but there's enough depth to get by — the early-season favorite to be that team.

teams.synopsis: Elite despite injuries to Keenan and Mostert — Nabers already looking like the real deal.
teams.blurb: Proving to be an elite team despite injuries to <mark class="hl-player">Keenan</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Mostert</mark> (6th- and 7th-round picks). <mark class="hl-player">Nabers</mark> looks like the real deal (28.7 points in Week 2). Even with down weeks from <mark class="hl-player">Josh Allen</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Ford</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Kincaid</mark>, the team was still able to put up 110+ points. 31 points from kicker + D/ST in Week 2 was a good boost, but shouldn't be counted on every week.

teams.synopsis: Solidifying himself in the top 3 for a second straight week — high floor even with kicker and D/ST at 3 points.
teams.blurb: Solidifying himself in the top 3 for the second straight week. <mark class="hl-player">Marvin Harrison Jr.</mark> took a week to get going but seems to be a top-12 wide receiver rest of season. Able to score 100+ points despite kicker + D/ST combining for 3 points, showing a high floor. <mark class="hl-player">Diggs</mark> will be inconsistent this season, but those boom weeks will win the team some matchups.

teams.synopsis: The top 4 looks pretty solidified — this is the start of the 'elite teams' tier.
teams.blurb: The top 4 seems pretty solidified in my opinion — in other words, Brandon's team is the beginning of the 'elite teams.' A great overall week from all of this team's players, except <mark class="hl-player">White</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Parkinson</mark>. <mark class="hl-player">Njoku</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark>, and White's injuries will be very important to monitor in the coming weeks. At full health, the team has top-3 upside, but even with the injuries it can contend for the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: In the 5th spot for the second straight week, on the strength of just enough production to keep faith alive.
teams.blurb: In the 5th spot for the second straight week, even though I said he wouldn't be... Not a high-scoring performance, but just enough for me to still have faith this team can have great weeks. The <mark class="hl-player">Tua</mark> injury will decrease <mark class="hl-player">Waddle</mark>'s production, as we've seen in the past. <mark class="hl-player">Mike Evans</mark> may be touchdown-dependent, but Anthony will need him to be great in Week 3 against a tough opponent.

teams.synopsis: Just outside the top 5 now — the Adams and Lamb duo is proving elite, and an excellent trade sets up more.
teams.blurb: Moving back up the rankings, Quin's team finds itself just outside the top 5. The duo of <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Lamb</mark> is proving to be elite (WR10 and WR16 respectively). An excellent trade sets the team up to excel even with <mark class="hl-player">Love</mark> out for some time and <mark class="hl-player">Pickens</mark> underperforming. The team is shaping up to be a contender when fully healthy.

teams.synopsis: Lost by just 1.3 points in a nail-biter — the Amon-Ra and Puka injuries are the ones to watch.
teams.blurb: A nail-biter in Week 2 saw Grits lose by just 1.3 points, but not all hope is lost. The <mark class="hl-player">Amon-Ra</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Puka</mark> injuries are important to monitor, the latter being out for at least 3 more weeks. Although Grits was only able to put up just under 100 points for the week, I expect bounce-back games from half the starting lineup, including <mark class="hl-player">Pitts</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">McConkey</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Moss</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Richardson</mark>.

teams.synopsis: A Week 2 loss drops this team to 0-2, but the roster's talent still says patience is warranted.
teams.blurb: A loss in Week 2 does push this team to 0-2 to start the year, but I still have faith. FKP is set up to only get better as the season goes on, with <mark class="hl-player">Thomas Jr.</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Moore</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Chubb</mark> all having better situations in the future. <mark class="hl-player">Swift</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Stroud</mark> have been disappointing in the first two weeks, but if Deniz can get solid production out of them, this team can start to win a few weeks.

teams.synopsis: A good Week 2 win moves this team up a spot, but the Pacheco injury could be a real detriment.
teams.blurb: A good win in Week 2 sees this team rise, if only by one spot, in the rankings. The injury to <mark class="hl-player">Pacheco</mark> may be detrimental, since he was Ryan's 1st-round pick and the RB15 in the first two weeks, but <mark class="hl-player">Jordan Mason</mark>'s emergence will provide support for the time being. <mark class="hl-player">LaPorta</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">McLaurin</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Cooper</mark> have been disappointing, but if they get on track, this team will rise.

teams.synopsis: The RB duo of Rhamondre and the Seahawks' starter combined for 34.9 — the WRs are the real holdup.
teams.blurb: The team may be settling in early as a bubble playoff team. The running back duo of Rhamondre and the starting Seahawks running back is becoming great, combining for 34.9 points in Week 2. The wide receivers are holding this team back from potentially being a top-5 team. Trades may be necessary for this team to become great, but the foundation has been set.

teams.synopsis: Genuinely unsure where this team lands this year — Kittle is showing out, but the RBs remain mid.
teams.blurb: Truthfully, I don't quite know this team's place in the league. Will it be a borderline playoff team, just outside of playoffs, or in contention for punishment? <mark class="hl-player">Kittle</mark> showed out in Week 2 (20.6 points) and may continue to, with <mark class="hl-player">Deebo</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">CMC</mark> being injured. <mark class="hl-player">Wilson</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Olave</mark> aren't showing their upside early on, and the running backs continue to be mid — however <mark class="hl-player">Javonte</mark> may be something.

teams.synopsis: Injuries to Kupp and AJ severely limit this team's win potential — Cook and McBride are the only bright spots.
teams.blurb: Injuries to <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">AJ</mark> severely limit this team's potential to win in the coming weeks. <mark class="hl-player">Dell</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Diontae</mark> have been disappointing (WR65 and WR75). The team is primed for a down year unless trades are made or players begin to overperform. Currently, <mark class="hl-player">Cook</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">McBride</mark> have been the only positives on the team.

teams.synopsis: The WRs continue to underperform outside of Ridley — a low floor and low ceiling through two weeks.
teams.blurb: The wide receivers continue to underperform, aside from <mark class="hl-player">Ridley</mark> (24.7 points in Week 2). <mark class="hl-player">Kelce</mark> looks to be one of the bigger busts of the year (TE1 in the draft). <mark class="hl-player">Kyren</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">JT</mark> have been solid, but not worth top-20 picks. Through the first two weeks, this team has shown a low floor and a low ceiling — not a good sign if they want to make the playoffs again.

teams.synopsis: Leaning on Tyreek for 20+ every week to have a shot — the RB trio is 2nd-worst in the league.
teams.blurb: Team relies on <mark class="hl-player">Tyreek</mark> to put up 20+ to have a chance at winning. Running back trio of <mark class="hl-player">Robinson Jr.</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Zeke</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Zamir</mark> is 2nd-worst in the league (RB14, RB31, RB45). The team's ceiling lowers every week as <mark class="hl-player">Burrow</mark>, Zamir, and <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> don't provide return on investment (4th round, 5th round, and 3rd round respectively).
